title: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
subtitle: >90% of pancreatic cancers (PNET <5%) · median age 71 · 60–70% arise in the head · 5-yr relative survival — localized 44%, regional 16%, distant 3%; 13% all stages, 8% for adenocarcinoma
source: Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Pancreatic Cancer (Johnson T, Lee W) · NCCN v2.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter

blocks.heading: Workup — all patients
items: Pancreatic-protocol CT chest/abdomen/pelvis — required for staging and resectability
MRI for indeterminate liver lesions or local extent
Germline testing in ALL patients regardless of family history — ~10% harbor a mutation
Tumor genomic profiling in all metastatic patients
Manage at a high-volume center with multidisciplinary input

blocks.heading: Presentation
items: Early: weight loss, nausea, bloating, abdominal pain
“Painless jaundice” is common but by no means universal
† New-onset diabetes in an older adult; migratory thrombophlebitis
† CA 19-9 pitfalls: falsely elevated by biliary obstruction — recheck after decompression; 5–10% are Lewis-antigen negative and never secrete it

blocks.heading: Staging — AJCC 8th
rows: celiac axis, SMA, or common hepatic artery — regardless of size
blocks.footnote: In practice resectability — not TNM — drives management: resectable · borderline · unresectable localized · metastatic. The call belongs to a hepatobiliary surgeon experienced with the Whipple.

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: daraxonrasib, 2L metastatic — median OS 13.2 vs 6.6 mo in RAS G12-mutant (NEJM 2026)

boxes: no RCT vs adjuvant — see note below
poor PS: single agent gem, 5-FU, capecitabine

blocks.html:
Neoadjuvant therapy has no RCT support. No prospective trial shows it beats adjuvant therapy; use is extrapolated from PRODIGE-24 and justified because it identifies bad biology before a morbid operation and gives early systemic control.

Two comparisons never made head-to-head: adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX vs gem/capecitabine, and first-line metastatic mFOLFIRINOX vs gem/nab-paclitaxel — choose by performance status.

blocks.heading: Regimens & dosing
blocks.footnote: All doses mg/m² unless stated. PRODIGE-24 used irinotecan 180 mg/m², reduced to 150 mg/m² — preplanned subgroup analysis showed equal efficacy.

blocks.heading: Biomarker → therapy
rows: Daraxonrasib — oral multi-selective RAS(ON) inhibitor; metastatic disease after ≥1 prior line, or not a candidate for multiagent therapy
Olaparib 300 mg PO BID — maintenance after ≥16 wk platinum (POLO)
Selpercatinib 120 mg BID (<50 kg) or 160 mg BID (≥50 kg)
blocks.footnote: Actionable alterations were historically rare — daraxonrasib changes that, since ~90% of PDAC is KRAS-mutant. Still profile every metastatic patient for the remainder.

blocks.heading: Surveillance after resection
items: H&P q3–6 months × 2 years, then q6–12 months
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast q3–6 months × 2 years, then q6–12 months
Signatera or equivalent ctDNA q3–6 months if indicated

blocks.heading: Supportive care
items: Nutrition referral · palliative care for all metastatic patients · hospice as appropriate
† Pancreatic enzyme replacement (PERT) — chronically underprescribed; exocrine insufficiency drives weight loss and treatment intolerance
† VTE prophylaxis — among the highest-risk malignancies for thrombosis
† Biliary stenting for obstruction · celiac plexus neurolysis for refractory pain

The call belongs to a hepatobiliary surgeon experienced with the Whipple. Key trials PRODIGE-24 adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX — OS 54.4 vs 35.0 mo (NEJM 2018) ESPAC-4 adjuvant gem + capecitabine (Lancet 2017) PRODIGE-4 FOLFIRINOX in metastatic disease (NEJM 2011) MPACT gem + nab-paclitaxel (NEJM 2013) POLO olaparib maintenance, germline BRCA (NEJM 2019) KEYNOTE-158 pembrolizumab in MSI-H (JCO 2020) RASolute 302 daraxonrasib, 2L metastatic — median OS 13.2 vs 6.6 mo in RAS G12-mutant (NEJM 2026) Treatment pathway Resectable or borderline Neoadjuvant chemotherapy FOLFIRINOX strongly preferred gem + nab-paclitaxel if PS limits no RCT vs adjuvant — see note below Surgery resection at a high-volume center Adjuvant chemotherapy mFOLFIRINOX (PRODIGE-24) preferred gem + capecitabine if moderate PS start ≤12 wk; 6 months total perioperative Surveillance see surveillance panel at right Unresectable or metastatic First line by performance status robust PS: FOLFIRINOX or NALIRIFOX moderate PS: gem + nab-paclitaxel poor PS: single agent gem, 5-FU, capecitabine Maintenance olaparib if germline BRCA1/2, no progression after 16 wk platinum (POLO) Second line RAS G12-mutant (~90%): daraxonrasib OS 13.2 vs 6.6 mo (RASolute 302) otherwise switch backbone Biomarker-directed therapy see biomarker table at right Neoadjuvant therapy has no RCT support. No prospective trial shows it beats adjuvant therapy; use is extrapolated from PRODIGE-24 and justified because it identifies bad biology before a morbid operation and gives early systemic control. Two comparisons never made head-to-head: adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX vs gem/capecitabine, and first-line metastatic mFOLFIRINOX vs gem/nab-paclitaxel — choose by performance status .
